tests.title: The rebuild creates its worktree with WorktreeAdd at an absolute <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id> path on the upstream base SHA
given: a mockGitRunner recording typed calls
a context carrying job ID 'job-42'
WorkspaceRoot is a relative path such as 'ws'
tests.when: HandleRebuildJob runs up to patch application
then: WorktreeAdd is called once on the trunk runner
the path argument is absolute, equals filepath.Abs('ws/<slug>/rebuild/job-42')
the commit argument is the SHA returned by resolveUpstreamBase
the call is the `git worktree add --detach` form
tests.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctxWithJobID('job-42'), job); c = mock.calls('WorktreeAdd')[0]; assert filepath.IsAbs(c.path); assert c.path == abs('ws/slug/rebuild/job-42'); assert c.sha == baseSHA

tests.title: A missing job ID yields a random ID and an empty WorkspaceRoot derives the path from the trunk's parent
given: a mockGitRunner
a context without a job ID
WorkspaceRoot is empty and the trunk path is <tmp>/<slug>/trunk
tests.when: HandleRebuildJob is run twice
then: both worktree paths are <tmp>/<slug>/rebuild/<id> with a non-empty id
the two ids differ
no error is returned because of the empty root
tests.pseudocode: p1 = pathOf(run()); p2 = pathOf(run()); assert dir(p1) == tmp+'/slug/rebuild'; assert base(p1) != '' ; assert p1 != p2

tests.title: Patch application goes through a worktree runner built after the directory exists; the trunk runner is limited to its allowed commands
given: a RebuildHandler whose NewGitRunner records the path argument and whether the directory existed at call time
a mock worktree runner and a mock trunk runner each recording commands
one rebase patch and one merge patch
tests.when: a rebuild runs to completion
then: NewGitRunner is called with the worktree path and the directory exists at that moment
log, cherry-pick, merge, rerere, diff --diff-filter=U, commit --no-edit and HEAD reads are recorded only on the worktree runner
the trunk runner records only fetch-adjacent reads, config, worktree add/remove/prune, update-ref and rev-parse
tests.pseudocode: assert worktreeRunner.commands ⊇ {log, cherry-pick, merge}; assert trunkRunner.commands ∩ {cherry-pick, merge, log --right-only, commit} == ∅

tests.title: The worktree directory and registration are gone after success, conflict, transient failure and cancellation
given: a real git repository workspace with an upstream remote and patch branches
a conflicting patch branch for the conflict case
a failure injected for the transient case and a cancelled context for the cancellation case
tests.when: a rebuild is run for each of the four outcomes
then: <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id> does not exist afterwards
`git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk
the outcomes are success, conflict result, TransientError, TransientError respectively
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in [success, conflict, transient, cancel]: run(scenario); assert !exists(wtPath); assert lines(git('worktree list')) == 1

tests.title: For any exit path the worktree is removed and pruned
given: a mockGitRunner that can inject an error at any step
tests.when: for any injection point chosen from every step between worktree creation and return (including no injection and a cancelled context)
then: WorktreeRemove is called followed by WorktreePrune whenever WorktreeAdd succeeded
the worktree directory does not exist at return
tests.pseudocode: for step in allSteps+[none,cancel]: run(inject(step)); if mock.added: assert mock.calls.endsWith(['WorktreeRemove','WorktreePrune']) ; assert !exists(path)

tests.title: A failing git worktree remove falls back to RemoveAll and prune, logs a warning and leaves the job outcome unchanged
given: a mockGitRunner whose WorktreeRemove returns an error
a real temp directory standing in for the worktree path
a captured logger
tests.when: a successful rebuild completes
then: os.RemoveAll removed the directory
WorktreePrune is called after the failed remove
a warning-level log entry names the slug and the path
the job result and returned error equal those of a run with successful removal
tests.pseudocode: r1 = run(removeOK); r2 = run(removeFails); assert r1 == r2; assert warnLogs contains slug and path; assert !exists(path)

tests.title: Cleanup runs with a non-cancelled context carrying a deadline of at most two minutes
given: a mockGitRunner that records ctx.Err() and ctx.Deadline() on WorktreeRemove and WorktreePrune
a job context that is cancelled mid-application
tests.when: the rebuild reacts to the cancellation
then: ctx.Err() is nil in the cleanup calls
a deadline exists and is no more than two minutes ahead
the worktree removal actually executed
tests.pseudocode: assert rec.removeCtxErr == nil; assert rec.deadline - now <= 2*time.Minute

tests.title: Typed worktree methods exist on GitRunner, the adapter and the mock, and MergeNoFF honours its message parameter
given: a real temporary git repository with two diverging branches
gitcmd.GitRunner, GitRunnerAdapter and mockGitRunner compiled against the carrypatch.GitRunner interface
tests.when: WorktreeAdd, WorktreePrune and WorktreeRemove are called through the adapter, then MergeNoFF is called with a message and with an empty message
then: the worktree is created, listed, removed and pruned
the merge with a message has that message as the commit subject
the merge with an empty message has git's default message
the interface assertion `var _ GitRunner = (*mockGitRunner)(nil)` compiles
tests.pseudocode: a.WorktreeAdd(ctx,p,sha); a.WorktreeRemove(ctx,p); a.WorktreePrune(ctx); a.MergeNoFF(ctx,'b',"Merge branch 'b'"); assert subject(HEAD)=="Merge branch 'b'"

tests.title: A failed worktree creation stops the run, leaves nothing, and returns an error
given: a mockGitRunner whose WorktreeAdd returns an error
a captured audit sink
a database with patch rows
tests.when: HandleRebuildJob runs
then: a non-nil error is returned
no cherry-pick, merge or UpdateRef call was made
no patch rows changed
no directory exists under rebuild/ for this run
RebuildActive(slug) is false and the lock is free
hub.rebuild.fail is emitted
tests.pseudocode: err = run(); assert err != nil; assert mock.calls('UpdateRef')==0; assert !wslock.RebuildActive(slug); assert tryLock(slug)

tests.title: The trunk runner runs no checkout, reset, cherry-pick, merge or rebase in the ordinary path, and legacy functions are gone
given: a mockGitRunner recording trunk commands
no _rebuild_temp branch and the trunk not on the integration branch
the rebuild_executor.go source
tests.when: a successful rebuild and a conflict rebuild run, and the source is scanned
then: the trunk runner records none of checkout, reset, cherry-pick, merge, rebase
the branch _rebuild_temp is never created
the source contains no function currentCheckout, restoreCheckout or preflightCleanup
tests.pseudocode: assert trunk.cmds ∩ {checkout,reset,cherry-pick,merge,rebase}==∅; assert !grep('func (currentCheckout|restoreCheckout|preflightCleanup)')

tests.title: The trunk's HEAD, status and sample file are identical before and after success, fail-fast conflict, continue-mode conflict and cancellation
given: a real git workspace whose trunk is checked out on a non-integration branch with a tracked sample file
patch branches including a conflicting one
tests.when: a rebuild is run for each of success, fail-fast conflict, continue-mode conflict and cancelled run
then: `git symbolic-ref HEAD` is identical to before
`git rev-parse HEAD` is identical to before
`git status --porcelain` output is identical to before
the sample file bytes are identical to before
tests.pseudocode: before = snap(trunk); run(scenario); assert snap(trunk) == before

tests.title: For any rebuild outcome the trunk checkout is unchanged
given: a real git workspace with a trunk checked out on a branch other than the integration branch
tests.when: for any generated patch set (1–5 patches, each clean, conflicting or missing), any strategy, any fail mode and optionally a cancellation point
then: symbolic-ref HEAD, rev-parse HEAD, status --porcelain and the sample file content are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for cfg in gen(): before=snap(trunk); run(cfg); assert snap(trunk)==before

tests.title: The integration branch is updated with update-ref to the worktree HEAD SHA and never with branch -f
given: a mockGitRunner whose worktree HEAD returns SHA 'abc123'
tests.when: phase two runs
then: UpdateRef is called on the trunk runner with refs/heads/<integration> and 'abc123'
no `branch -f` or checkout of the integration branch is recorded
tests.pseudocode: assert mock.calls('UpdateRef')[0] == ('refs/heads/'+integ,'abc123'); assert no call has args ['branch','-f',...]

tests.title: The previous integration head is read immediately before the update under the lock and recorded, empty when absent
given: a mockGitRunner recording call order and lock state
two cases: the integration branch exists at SHA 'old1' and it does not exist
tests.when: phase two runs in each case
then: rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<integration> immediately precedes UpdateRef while the lock is held
previous_integration_head_sha is 'old1' in the first case and empty in the second
tests.pseudocode: assert order == [rev-parse --verify, UpdateRef]; assert lockHeld at both; assert result.prev == 'old1' / ''

tests.title: The trunk is hard-reset only when its HEAD is the integration branch
given: a real git workspace
case 1: the trunk has the integration branch checked out
case 2: the trunk is on another branch
a captured logger
tests.when: a successful rebuild runs in each case
then: case 1: after the run the trunk's files and index match the new integration tip, `git status --porcelain` is empty, and an info log entry records the reset
case 2: no reset is run in the trunk and the trunk is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: case1: assert git(trunk,'rev-parse HEAD')==newTip; assert status==''; assert infoLog('reset'); case2: assert trunkCmds ∩ {reset}==∅

tests.title: A leftover _rebuild_temp branch is deleted and logged in phase one
given: a real git workspace whose trunk is on another branch
a local refs/heads/_rebuild_temp
a captured logger
tests.when: a rebuild runs
then: `git show-ref refs/heads/_rebuild_temp` finds nothing
an info log entry carrying the slug records the removal
the branch is not recreated during the run
tests.pseudocode: run(); assert exitCode(git('show-ref','refs/heads/_rebuild_temp'))!=0; assert infoLog contains slug

tests.title: A trunk left on _rebuild_temp mid-cherry-pick is moved to the workspace branch, else origin/HEAD, else detached, before the branch is deleted
given: a real git workspace whose trunk is on _rebuild_temp with an in-progress conflicted cherry-pick
three variants: workspaceBranch exists locally; it is unset but refs/remotes/origin/HEAD resolves to a local branch; neither exists
tests.when: a rebuild runs in each variant
then: the in-progress operation is aborted
variant 1: trunk HEAD is on workspaceBranch
variant 2: trunk HEAD is on the short name of origin/HEAD
variant 3: trunk HEAD is detached and a warning is logged
_rebuild_temp no longer exists in all variants
tests.pseudocode: for v in variants: setup(v); run(); assert symbolicRef(trunk)==expected(v); assert !branchExists('_rebuild_temp')

tests.title: A failing update-ref stops phase two before bookkeeping or push, releases the lock and returns an error
given: a mockGitRunner whose UpdateRef fails
a database with merged_upstream and active patches and a PushIntegration spy
tests.when: HandleRebuildJob runs
then: a non-nil error is returned
no patch row is soft-deleted or re-positioned
PushIntegration was not called
the workspace lock is free afterwards
hub.rebuild.fail is emitted
tests.pseudocode: err=run(); assert err!=nil; assert rowsUnchanged(); assert push.calls==0; assert tryLock(slug)

tests.title: rerere config is set on the trunk runner before the worktree is added and extensions.worktreeConfig is never enabled
given: a mockGitRunner recording call order
tests.when: a rebuild runs
then: config rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true are issued on the trunk runner before WorktreeAdd
no config call mentions extensions.worktreeConfig
tests.pseudocode: assert idx('config rerere.enabled true') < idx('WorktreeAdd'); assert idx('config rerere.autoupdate true') < idx('WorktreeAdd'); assert none(args contains 'worktreeConfig')

tests.title: A resolution recorded in one rebuild's worktree is replayed with no conflict in the next rebuild
given: a real git workspace with two patch branches that conflict on the same hunk
a first rebuild that conflicts, after which the conflict is resolved in its worktree and recorded in rr-cache
tests.when: a second rebuild of the same workspace runs
then: the conflicting patch is reported as success rather than conflict
the result tree contains the recorded resolution
tests.pseudocode: run1(); resolveAndRecord(); r=run2(); assert r.patch[1].status=='success'

tests.title: The rerere endpoints list a resolution recorded in a rebuild worktree and DELETE forgets it
given: a real workspace with an HTTP router wired to the rerere handlers
one resolution recorded by a rebuild worktree into the common rr-cache
tests.when: GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere, then DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rerere/<entry>, then GET again
then: the first GET is 200 and lists the entry
DELETE succeeds
the second GET does not list the entry and the rr-cache directory for it is gone from <trunk>/.git/rr-cache
tests.pseudocode: assert entry in get().entries; assert delete(entry).status==200; assert entry not in get().entries

tests.title: For any set of recorded resolutions the endpoints list and forget each one
given: a real workspace and rerere handlers
tests.when: for any 1–4 distinct conflict resolutions recorded in rebuild worktrees and any deletion order
then: GET lists exactly the entries not yet deleted
each deleted entry is absent from the following GET
tests.pseudocode: for set,order in gen(): record(set); for e in order: delete(e); assert get() == set - deleted

tests.title: Discarding a worktree mid-conflict leaves rr-cache and the trunk's MERGE_RR unaffected
given: a real workspace with one previously recorded resolution
a rebuild that stops on a conflict so MERGE_RR is populated in the worktree
tests.when: the rebuild ends and discards the worktree, then GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere is called
then: GET returns 200 with the entries recorded before the discard
<trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR has no entry from the discarded worktree (absent or empty)
tests.pseudocode: assert get().status==200; assert entriesBefore ⊆ get().entries; assert read(trunk/.git/MERGE_RR)==''

tests.title: Credentials are resolved first, then the blocking lock is taken and BeginRebuild is called under it
given: spies for credential resolution, wslock.Lock and BeginRebuild recording order and lock state
tests.when: HandleRebuildJob starts
then: order is credentials, Lock, BeginRebuild
BeginRebuild observed the lock held
tests.pseudocode: assert order==['creds','Lock','BeginRebuild']; assert lockHeldDuring(BeginRebuild)

tests.title: A credential failure returns a TransientError before locking or setting the guard
given: credential resolution returning an error
a captured audit sink
tests.when: HandleRebuildJob runs
then: the error is a TransientError
tryLock(slug) succeeds
RebuildActive(slug) is false
hub.rebuild.fail is emitted
tests.pseudocode: err=run(); var te *TransientError; assert errors.As(err,&te); assert !wslock.RebuildActive(slug); assert tryLock(slug)

tests.title: Phase one performs its steps in order under the lock and then unlocks
given: a mock runner and spies recording order and lock state
tests.when: a rebuild runs phase one
then: order is fetch, trunk runner creation, resolveUpstreamBase, _rebuild_temp migration, stale cleanup, rerere config
the lock is held for every step and released before WorktreeAdd
tests.pseudocode: assert order==[fetch,newRunner,resolveBase,migrate,staleCleanup,rerereConfig]; assert allLocked; assert !locked(at WorktreeAdd)

tests.title: Sync, rollback and rerere forget succeed while a rebuild is blocked inside a patch step and the lock is free
given: a fake runner that blocks inside a cherry-pick until released
real sync, rollback and rerere-forget handlers
the rebuild started in a goroutine
tests.when: while the rebuild is blocked, POST /sync, a rollback and a rerere forget are sent, then the rebuild is released
then: TryLock(slug) succeeds while blocked
sync responds with its normal success status, not 409 workspace_busy, and updates upstream_head_sha
rollback and rerere forget succeed
the rebuild keeps the base SHA resolved in phase one and completes
tests.pseudocode: go run(); <-blocked; assert tryLock(slug); assert post('/sync').status==200; assert rollback().status==200; assert forget().status==200; release()

tests.title: Phase two re-acquires the lock for ref update, bookkeeping and push, then releases it
given: a mock runner, a PushIntegration spy and a database with merged_upstream patches
tests.when: phase two runs
then: Lock is acquired a second time after patch application
previous-head read, UpdateRef, soft-deletion, compaction and PushIntegration all happen with the lock held in that order
the lock is released afterwards
tests.pseudocode: assert order==[lock,readPrev,updateRef,softDelete,compact,push,unlock]

tests.title: For any early return in phase one or two the lock is released and worktree work runs outside any lock
given: a mock runner that can fail at any step
tests.when: for any failure injected at any step of phase one, worktree creation, application, or phase two
then: tryLock(slug) succeeds after HandleRebuildJob returns
WorktreeAdd, patch application and WorktreeRemove never run while the lock is held
tests.pseudocode: for step in allSteps: run(failAt(step)); assert tryLock(slug); assert !lockedDuring(worktree ops)

tests.title: A rollback during patch application is overwritten by the rebuild's update-ref and previous head records the rolled-back SHA
given: a real workspace whose integration branch is at SHA 'A'
a rebuild blocked mid-application
a rollback target SHA 'R'
tests.when: rollback to 'R' completes during application and the rebuild is then released
then: the integration branch equals the rebuild's final worktree HEAD SHA
previous_integration_head_sha equals 'R'
tests.pseudocode: rollback('R'); release(); assert rev('integration')==finalSHA; assert result.prev=='R'

tests.title: After phase two the order is worktree removal, stale check, complete event, guard end, return
given: spies recording order for WorktreeRemove, stale-input check, audit emit and the end() call
tests.when: a successful rebuild finishes
then: order is WorktreeRemove, stale check, hub.rebuild.complete, end guard
RebuildActive(slug) is true until the complete event
tests.pseudocode: assert order==[remove,staleCheck,emit('hub.rebuild.complete'),end]

tests.title: BeginRebuild sets a flag independent of the mutex and its end function is idempotent
given: a fresh wslock instance
tests.when: BeginRebuild('a') is called while the mutex is free, end() is called twice, and a second guard is set between the two end() calls
then: RebuildActive('a') is true after BeginRebuild and Lock/TryLock behaviour is unaffected
RebuildActive('a') is false after the first end()
the second end() does not clear a guard set later by another run
tests.pseudocode: end,ok=BeginRebuild('a'); assert ok&&RebuildActive('a'); assert TryLock('a'); end(); assert !Active; _,ok2=Begin('a'); end(); assert Active('a')

tests.title: BeginRebuild on an already guarded slug returns false and the rebuild returns a retryable error
given: a guard already set for slug 'a'
tests.when: BeginRebuild('a') is called directly, and HandleRebuildJob runs for 'a'
then: BeginRebuild returns ok=false with a non-nil callable end
the existing guard remains set
HandleRebuildJob returns a retryable TransientError
the lock is free afterwards
tests.pseudocode: end,ok=Begin('a'); assert !ok; end(); assert Active('a'); err=run(); assert isTransient(err); assert tryLock('a')

tests.title: The guard is held from before stale cleanup until after worktree removal on every exit path
given: spies observing RebuildActive at stale cleanup, WorktreeAdd and WorktreeRemove
success, patch-conflict and error scenarios
tests.when: a rebuild runs in each scenario
then: RebuildActive is true at stale cleanup and after WorktreeRemove completes
RebuildActive is false after HandleRebuildJob returns in all scenarios
tests.pseudocode: for s in scenarios: run(s); assert activeAt('staleCleanup') && activeAt('afterRemove'); assert !Active(slug)

tests.title: Archive of a ready workspace returns 409 workspace_busy while the guard is set and the lock is free
given: a ready workspace and the real archive handler
wslock guard set via BeginRebuild with the mutex free
tests.when: the archive endpoint is called
then: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy
the workspace is not archived
TryLock(slug) succeeds afterwards
tests.pseudocode: BeginRebuild(slug); r=archive(); assert r.status==409; assert r.json.error_type=='workspace_busy'; assert !isArchived(slug); assert tryLock(slug)

tests.title: Reclone returns 409 workspace_busy while the guard is set, leaving the clone directory untouched
given: a ready workspace with a trunk directory and the real reclone handler
the guard set and the mutex free
tests.when: the reclone endpoint is called
then: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy
the trunk directory and its contents are untouched
TryLock(slug) succeeds afterwards
tests.pseudocode: BeginRebuild(slug); r=reclone(); assert r.status==409; assert exists(trunk/marker); assert tryLock(slug)

tests.title: Archive and reclone behave as before once the guard has been ended
given: a ready workspace, a guard set then ended with end()
tests.when: archive and (on another workspace) reclone are requested
then: archive succeeds with its normal success status and the workspace is archived
reclone is accepted with its normal success status
tests.pseudocode: end,_=Begin(slug); end(); assert archive().status==200; assert reclone(other).status==202

tests.title: Sync, rollback and rerere forget are not rejected by the guard when the lock is free
given: the guard set for the workspace and the mutex free
real sync, rollback and rerere-forget handlers
tests.when: each endpoint is called
then: none of them returns 409 workspace_busy
each returns its normal success status
tests.pseudocode: BeginRebuild(slug); for ep in [sync,rollback,forget]: assert ep().status != 409

tests.title: Patch tips are resolved to SHAs with rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<branch>^{commit} in the trunk runner and only SHAs are used afterwards
given: a mock trunk runner returning SHAs per branch
patches with statuses active, merged_upstream, disabled and deleted
a branch that moves in the mock after the snapshot
tests.when: a rebuild runs
then: rev-parse --verify is called only for non-merged_upstream/disabled/deleted patches, on the trunk runner, with refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}
the resolution happens after sorting and before the first patch application
log, cherry-pick and merge arguments contain the snapshot SHA and never the branch name
tests.pseudocode: assert trunk.calls('rev-parse --verify')==activeBranches; assert none(worktree.args contains branchName)

tests.title: The rebase strategy lists commits with git log ... <base>...<snapshot sha> in the worktree
given: a rebase-strategy patch with snapshot SHA 'sha1' and base 'base1'
a mock worktree runner
tests.when: the patch is applied
then: the worktree runner receives log --reverse --no-merges --right-only --cherry-pick base1...sha1
tests.pseudocode: assert worktree.args('log')==['log','--reverse','--no-merges','--right-only','--cherry-pick','base1...sha1']

tests.title: A merge-strategy patch merges the snapshot SHA while naming the branch in the commit message
given: a real workspace with a merge-strategy patch branch 'feature/x'
tests.when: a rebuild runs
then: the worktree merge is invoked with the SHA and the message "Merge branch 'feature/x'"
the integration branch tip commit message contains 'feature/x'
tests.pseudocode: run(); assert git('log -1 --format=%B integration') contains 'feature/x'

tests.title: An unresolvable or empty-resolving branch, or an empty rebase commit list, is skipped with branch_not_found without failing the run
given: three patches: rev-parse errors, rev-parse returns empty output, and a rebase patch whose log is empty
a fourth healthy patch after them
tests.when: HandleRebuildJob runs
then: patch_results has status skipped and reason branch_not_found for the three patches
the healthy patch is applied with status success
the job does not return an error
tests.pseudocode: r,err=run(); assert err==nil; assert r.patches[0..2] all skipped/branch_not_found; assert r.patches[3].status=='success'

tests.title: A tag or remote-tracking ref with the patch's name is not matched
given: a real workspace where tag 'p1' and refs/remotes/origin/p2 exist but no refs/heads/p1 or refs/heads/p2
tests.when: a rebuild runs with patches p1 and p2
then: both patches are recorded skipped with reason branch_not_found
tests.pseudocode: r=run(); assert r.patches[p1]==('skipped','branch_not_found'); assert r.patches[p2]==('skipped','branch_not_found')

tests.title: source_sha is set for snapshotted patches including conflicts, carried in result, progress and API JSON, and omitted when empty
given: a run with one success patch, one conflict patch (continue mode) and one disabled patch
a progress recorder and the rebuild API response encoder
tests.when: the run finishes and the result is marshalled
then: success and conflict patches carry their snapshot SHA in source_sha
the disabled patch's JSON has no source_sha key
the running job's progress snapshots include source_sha
the API response patch_results include source_sha
tests.pseudocode: assert json(r.patches[0]).source_sha==sha0; assert 'source_sha' not in json(r.patches[2]); assert progress.last.patches[0].source_sha==sha0

tests.title: For any patch branch that moves after its snapshot, exactly the snapshot's commits are applied and reported
given: a real workspace and a rebuild blocked after snapshotting
tests.when: for any branch movement after the snapshot (new commits pushed, branch reset, branch deleted)
then: the applied commits equal those reachable from the snapshot SHA only
source_sha equals the snapshot SHA
tests.pseudocode: for mv in gen(): snapshot; apply(mv); assert appliedCommits==log(base...snap); assert result.source_sha==snap

tests.title: The stale-input check marks moved patch tips and upstream base after worktree removal and phase-two unlock
given: a mock runner where success and conflict patch branches re-resolve to new SHAs, and a merged_upstream patch branch also moved
resolveUpstreamBase returning a different SHA the second time
a fail-fast conflict variant
tests.when: a successful run and a fail-fast conflict run end
then: the check runs after WorktreeRemove and with the lock free
only the success and conflict patches are marked stale; the merged_upstream patch is ignored
upstream is marked stale
the check also runs in the fail-fast conflict exit
tests.pseudocode: assert order==[unlock,remove,staleCheck]; assert stale.patches==['p1','p2']; assert stale.upstream

tests.title: Retryable errors, cancellation and other failures skip the check and enqueue no follow-up
given: moved patch tips and upstream
a real in-memory jobqueue and audit sink
tests.when: a run ends with a TransientError, a cancellation and a non-conflict failure
then: no job with submitted_by system:stale-snapshot exists
no hub.rebuild.followup event is emitted
tests.pseudocode: for s in [transient,cancel,otherFail]: run(s); assert queue.countBySubmitter('system:stale-snapshot')==0; assert audit.none('hub.rebuild.followup')

tests.title: A stale patch tip enqueues one follow-up unless AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is false
given: a run whose patch tip moved during the run
workspace variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH unset, then 'false'
tests.when: the run finishes in each configuration
then: with the variable unset exactly one follow-up is enqueued
with 'false' none is enqueued
tests.pseudocode: assert queue.count('system:stale-snapshot')==1 (unset); ==0 ('false')

tests.title: A stale upstream base enqueues one follow-up unless AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is false
given: a run during which resolveUpstreamBase changes
AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC unset, then 'false'
tests.when: the run finishes in each configuration
then: with the variable unset exactly one follow-up is enqueued
with 'false' none is enqueued
AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH='false' alone does not suppress an upstream follow-up
tests.pseudocode: assert count==1 (unset); ==0 (SYNC=false); ==1 (PUSH=false only)

tests.title: At most one follow-up is enqueued per run with the original payload, system submitter, fresh nonce and the running job's group key, and it stays queued
given: a real jobqueue with a running rebuild job whose GroupKey is 'g1'
both a stale patch and a stale upstream
tests.when: the rebuild finishes
then: exactly one new job exists
its type is rebuild, key is the slug, submitted_by is system:stale-snapshot
its payload strategy, fail mode and integration branch equal the original and its nonce differs
its GroupKey is 'g1' (FormatGroupKey fallback when GetByID fails)
its status is queued and it does not start before the current job is finalised
tests.pseudocode: fu=queue.listQueued(); assert len(fu)==1; assert fu[0].GroupKey=='g1'; assert fu[0].Payload.nonce != orig.nonce; assert fu[0].Status=='queued'

tests.title: ExcludeJobID makes both dedup queries ignore the named job and leaves dedup unchanged when empty
given: a real jobqueue database with a running job J of type 'rebuild' key 'k'

tests.pseudocode: assert Enqueue(p).ID==J; assert Enqueue(p+Exclude J).ID != J

tests.title: hub.rebuild.followup is emitted with stale_patches, upstream_stale and follow_up_job_id and is a registered audit query event type
